name: CoSchedule Headline Studio
tagline: Score headlines, email subject lines, and video titles on length, word balance, and sentiment

pricing.notes: Premium is priced on a credit slider. The entry price is the 10 credit step; credits are spent to generate and analyze headlines.
pricing.freeTier: The free Basic plan includes 10 credits to analyze headlines, with word balance, sentiment, and limited history.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: 10 credits, limited history and idea generation

pricing.hiddenCosts: Every analysis or generation spends a credit, so the real price depends on how many headlines you test.

verdictSummary: The part people open Headline Studio for is a scorer: count the words, sort them into common, uncommon, emotional, and power buckets, run sentiment, check length per format, and turn it into a number. That is word lists, a sentiment library, and a weighted sum, all of which run in a browser tab with no server. The score itself is a heuristic either way, so a home-made version with weights you can see is no less valid than the vendor's. What does not come along is the hosted extras: AI headline suggestions, keyword and competitor data, and the extension that scores titles inside WordPress, Gmail, and YouTube.
coreLoopDIY: Paste a headline, classify each word against local word lists, run sentiment and length checks per format, and show a weighted score with history.
whatYouLose: keyword suggestions and competitor analysis data
the browser extension and WordPress plugin that score titles where you write
a score people on your team already recognise
moatNotes: the extension and plugin reach, plus a familiar score
whyPeopleStillPay: The free tier already covers the scorer for light use, so people who pay are mostly buying volume, the AI suggestions, and the keyword data. A team that has used the score for years also has a shared habit around it, which a new tool has to replace.

notes: Entry price is the lowest Premium credit step; the free Basic plan is enough for occasional use.
prompt:
Build a personal headline checker in an empty folder as a single static web page.
Use plain TypeScript bundled with esbuild into one app.js, plus index.html and style.css; no framework and no backend.
The core loop is: paste a headline, pick a format (blog title, email subject line, YouTube title, ad headline), and see a word-by-word breakdown with plain checks.
Count words and characters per format and flag when the length is outside a sensible range for that format.
Classify each word as common, uncommon, emotional, or power using four editable JSON word lists shipped in /data.
Show the word balance as a simple bar and highlight each word in the headline by its class.
Score sentiment as positive, neutral, or negative with the MIT-licensed sentiment package (AFINN), bundled locally.
Detect headline type (list, how-to, question, statement) with small regex rules, and flag missing numbers or vague openers.
Preview the headline truncated as a Google result title and as an email subject in a narrow inbox row.
Combine the checks into a 0 to 100 score with the weights visible and editable in one config file.
Keep a local history of the last 200 headlines in localStorage with their scores, and allow export to CSV.
Allow comparing two headlines side by side.
Everything runs in the browser; nothing typed leaves the page.
Include clear empty and error states and keyboard-only use.
Write unit tests with node:test for the word classifier, length rules, and score weights.
Write a README covering how to edit the word lists and how to run it from file:// or npx serve.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or any network calls.
Deliberately leave out AI headline generation and keyword search volume.
Deliberately leave out the WordPress plugin and the browser extension.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
